metadata.title: Bundles
metadata.description: Detailed guide for managing Capgo Bundles, covering listing, deleting, bundle (version) management, and storage optimization for app update packages.

blocks.text: Bundles are the core update packages in Capgo. Each bundle contains the web assets (HTML, CSS, JS) that make up your app's content. The Bundles API allows you to manage these update packages, including listing and deleting them.
A bundle represents a specific bundle (version) of your app's web content and includes:
: Unique hash to verify bundle integrity
: Details about where and how the bundle is stored
: Creation time, ownership, and other tracking information

Step 4: Upload Bundle to Your Storage
Upload your zip file to any web-accessible storage:

# Example: Upload to your server via scp
scp my-app-1.2.3.zip user@your-server.com:/var/www/bundles/

# Example: Upload to S3 using AWS CLI
aws s3 cp my-app-1.2.3.zip s3://your-bucket/bundles/

# Example: Upload via curl to a custom endpoint
curl -X POST https://your-storage-api.com/upload \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -F "file=@my-app-1.2.3.zip"
via HTTPS URL (no authentication required). Capgo's servers need to download the bundle from this URL.
Step 5: Register Bundle with Capgo API
Register the external bundle with Capgo using direct API calls:

Your bundle zip must follow these requirements:
: Use relative paths for all assets

bundle.zip
├── index.html
├── assets/
│   ├── app.js
│   └── styles.css
└── images/

Use the exact same package and method that Capgo CLI uses internally:
: Ensures the bundle hasn't been corrupted during transfer
: Capgo verifies checksums before accepting bundles

: Set appropriate minimum native version requirements
Retrieve bundle information. Returns 50 bundles per page.
: Required. The ID of your app

interface Bundle {
  app_id: string
  bucket_id: string | null
  checksum: string | null
  created_at: string | null
  deleted: boolean
  external_url: string | null
  id: number
  minUpdateVersion: string | null
  name: string
  native_packages: Json[] | null
  owner_org: string
  r2_path: string | null
  session_key: string | null
  storage_provider: string
  updated_at: string | null
  user_id: string | null
}

# Get all bundles
curl -H "authorization: your-api-key" \
  "https://api.capgo.app/bundle/?app_id=app_123"

# Get next page
curl -H "authorization: your-api-key" \
  "https://api.capgo.app/bundle/?app_id=app_123&page=1"
Delete one or all bundles for an app. Use with caution as this action cannot be undone.

# Delete specific bundle
curl -X DELETE \
  -H "authorization: your-api-key" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "app_id": "app_123",
    "version": "1.0.0"
  }' \
  https://api.capgo.app/bundle/

# Delete all bundles
curl -X DELETE \
  -H "authorization: your-api-key" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "app_id": "app_123"
  }' \
  https://api.capgo.app/bundle/

    "comment": "Fixed critical bug in authentication"
